subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (next steps)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Desai <anita.desai@paymentsys.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (next steps)

Hi Anita —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured the right priorities and next steps. Please correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you called out:
- Recent multi-region failover exposed gaps in routing and cache warmup; customer-facing pages saw spike in latency and a 7% error rate during the March incident.
- Need predictable tail latency at peak (p99) for critical payment flows to avoid retries and duplicate charges.
- Limited ability to degrade gracefully: current fallback is a coarse region reroute which increases latency and impacts user experience.

What success looks like (your criteria):
- Availability: >= 99.95% for payment validation API under normal load.
- Latency: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms for LLM-powered enrichment calls.
- Graceful degradation plan that keeps core payments path readable/functional if model variants are degraded.
- Observable, auditable incident history and SLO reports for compliance reviews.

Current stack notes you shared:
- Primary: in-house HTTP gateway -> payments service -> enrichment worker calling LLMs in us-west and us-east.
- Existing model endpoints are a mix of hosted vendor X and a smaller on-prem model for low-latency traffic.
- Autoscaling for workers but no KV prefix caching for model responses today.

Reliability & graceful degradation levers we discussed (Redwood options):
- Model fallback hierarchy (low-latency local quantized variant -> regional hosted model -> reduced-feature cached response).
- Smart routing by policy (latency-first for payment flows, cost-tier fallback for batch enrichment).
- Automatic prefix/KV caching for hot prompts to reduce cold-starts during failover.
- Canary/traffic split rollouts and automatic revert when error budget breached.

Next steps (agreed):
1) You to share incident timeline and any post-mortem slides (Anita) — we requested March incident log export.
2) We’ll propose a canary plan for PaymentSys: fallback models, routing policy, and SLO mapping (Redwood) — deliver by Friday 5/22.
3) Intro call with our reliability engineer to scope a short POC (30-day) for the payments enrichment path (we suggested Tue 5/26).
4) Initial security/compliance checklist — we’ll attach SLO mapping template and our SRE playbook.

Attachments: redwood-slo-playbook.pdf, slo_requirements.xlsx (attached for reference).

If that looks right I’ll loop in Marissa (AE) and Elliot (reliability lead) to set dates and scope.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Hey Jordan —

Thanks for the thorough summary — that captures it well. A few clarifications and additional context:

Incident history:
- Root cause for the March 12 incident: control-plane throttling in our primary region caused a cascade of cold cache misses across enrichment workers; error spike lasted ~18 minutes, ~7% failed transactions across the enrichment path. We have a post-mortem deck I can share (PDF).
- We also had a smaller incident on 2026-04-08 where a model rollback changed output schema, which required a quick-fix and contributed to downstream errors.

SLO/Compliance expectations:
- For the payments enrichment path we need clear SLOs we can publish internally: availability and p99 latency commitments at the endpoint level.
- Any plan must include an audit trail and retention of request/response metadata (30-90 days) for dispute resolution.

Canary & fallback asks:
- Canary must start at <=1% of traffic, ramp to 10% with manual gate at 5% (we need the ability to pause).
- Fallback to a local quantized model is preferred to avoid cross-region latency when possible.

I’ll attach the post-mortem and the list of fields we need retained for disputes. I’m available Tue 5/26 morning PT for the intro with your reliability engineer — 9:30am PT works for me.

Anita
Head of Platform Reliability | PaymentSys
anita.desai@paymentsys.com

Attachment references: payment-march12-pm.pdf, payment-dispute-fields.csv

Looping in Marissa (AE) and Elliot (reliability lead) to scope the POC and finalize the canary/fallback plan.

Elliot — quick notes from the call and Anita’s asks below (I attached Anita’s post-mortem and the dispute fields CSV). High level ask: 30-day POC focused on payments enrichment where Redwood demonstrates:
- Canary plan: 1% -> manual gate at 5% -> 10% ramp, ability to pause and auto-revert on error budget breach.
- Fallback path: local quantized variant in us-west for latency-sensitive traffic, region fallback to us-east only if local capacity is exhausted.
- Observability: per-token latency and error metrics, audit log retention for 90 days for dispute fields.
- SLO proposals: availability >=99.95%, p99 <500ms for enrichment endpoints.

Attachments included: redwood-slo-playbook.pdf (Redwood SRE playbook), slo_requirements.xlsx (SLO mapping template), payment-march12-pm.pdf (PaymentSys post-mortem)

Marissa — can you pick a time for the intro call with Anita and confirm preferred stakeholders?

Thanks —
Jordan
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation (next steps)

Thanks for the context — jumping in. Quick take and proposed next steps from reliability/engineering: 

Initial proposal (what we can deliver in a 30-day POC):
- Deployment: provision a dedicated canary pool (us-west) with a quantized local model variant and a regional fallback (us-east hosted).
- Canary gating: implement traffic-split controller with manual gates at 1% start, stop/ramp controls at 5% and can automate rollback on error budget threshold (configurable).
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for hot prompts with warmup pre-seeding during failover windows.
- Observability & retention: we can export per-request metadata to your secure bucket for 90-day retention and provide a Kibana dashboard for p95/p99 and error rates.

Questions before we scope work:
1) For dispute retention, what specific fields do you need written to the audit log? (Anita you mentioned a CSV — thx).
2) Expected peak TPS for enrichment calls during payment processing windows (helps size canary pool).

Action items:
- Jordan/Marissa: schedule Tue 5/26 9:30am PT intro call with Anita and send calendar invite.
- Anita: share the post-mortem and the dispute-fields CSV (if possible before Fri 5/22).
- Elliot: I’ll draft a POC plan and estimate and share by EOD Friday 5/22.

Elliot Price
Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
elliot.price@redwood.ai
